title: ZIP Code Map: Plot a List of ZIPs
description: Plot a list of ZIP codes on a map with the ZIP Code Map — centroids, clusters and an optional heat layer from your own list. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, eight famous ZIP centroids — 10001, 02108, 20001, 60601, 30303, 33101, 90210, 94103 — plotted together sketch the country's postal skeleton from Manhattan to San Francisco.
quick_answer: The ZIP Code Map plots a pasted list of ZIP codes as points on a map, using each code's centroid, with clustering and an optional heat view. Paste your list and see its geography at once: where your customers and deliveries actually concentrate.
steps_intro: A column of ZIPs is a map waiting to happen:

body.t: The CRM export's ZIP column, plotted, is the cheapest market research in existence. Density questions go deeper with the
Territories drawn from a list look tidy in rows and ragged on a map. The plot is the audit — overlaps and orphan regions show themselves.
Plot served ZIPs against your depots (the
pattern) and the uncovered clusters argue for the next route.
Donor and member ZIPs reveal the natural geography of your community — chapters and events should follow the dots, not the alphabet.
Each ZIP plots at its centroid — the middle of its delivery area, not a boundary outline. Manhattan's 10001 and Beverly Hills' 90210 sit 2,453 miles apart as points; their areas' shapes are the
Where dots pile up, the heat layer glows. It displays the density of your list — not of population, not of income — a distinction the map's readers deserve to hear stated aloud.

popular_table.note: ZIP codes are mail-delivery constructs (and their map areas are Census ZCTAs, approximations) — the standing caveat of every ZIP tool on this site.

faq: No — it plots centroid points (and heat). Boundary shapes are approximations owned by the ZIP Code Boundary Viewer; conflating the two is the classic ZIP-map error.
One ZIP per line or comma-separated pastes both read naturally. Extra columns (city, counts) are ignored beyond the code itself unless a mode says otherwise.
Repeated ZIPs stack at one point — the heat view reads the pile-up as intensity, which is either your intent (weighted demand) or a cleaning task, depending on your data.
Can I colour by a value?
Where the list carries values, heat intensity is the value's picture. Categorical colouring belongs to choropleth tooling; this map's grammar is points and density.
Rural ZIPs are geographically huge and few per area; sparse dots over farmland are the honest picture, not missing data.
This map is US ZIP-shaped. UK and other systems have their own tools in the Location family (postcode distance and boundary tools among them).
The list is processed for the plot — but a plotted customer map is itself sensitive. Aggregate and share the picture at the zoom your ethics (and your privacy policy) allow.
